title: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1 - Ethics & Professional Responsibilities - Paralegal as Guarantor
exam: LSO Paralegal Ethics & Professional Responsibilities Practice Test 1
subject: Ethics & Professional Responsibilities

questions.q: A paralegal's client cannot afford bail for a provincial offence charge and asks the paralegal to act as their surety (guarantor) to the court. Is the paralegal ethically permitted to do this?
options: No, a paralegal must not act as a surety for, or personally guarantee a debt of, a client.
Yes, if the paralegal truly believes the client is innocent.
Yes, provided the client signs an indemnity agreement.
No, only lawyers can act as sureties.
questions.explain: Rule 3.06 outlines rules on transactions with clients, which generally prohibit a paralegal from acting as a surety for a client, guaranteeing a client's debts, or bailing them out, as it creates an unmanageable financial and personal conflict of interest.
